## CELL FACTS

Cell 土_伤官 (Earth carrying The Virtuoso). Persona The Virtuoso (伤官). Definition line: "Cross-current output, brilliance made of what it meets". Keyword Brilliance, charge fierce, poles catalyst Spark / friction Pushback. Family function: Expression. Cost dimension: brilliance against the grain; shining reads as defiance. Arena: the stage, spark, off-script, the note held too long. Classical portrait: brilliance and defiance; output that exceeds its container; 傲物气高, cannot hold its tongue. Ruled domains: Talent, Performance, Defiance. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 食神.
Element arena: Earth (ground, soil, load, field, bedrock, harvest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Fire generating Earth cross-polarity — warmth building structure beyond expectation".
- k2_overview: "Your Earth moves as the Virtuoso: ground that refuses to stay flat. You produce solid, startling things, the building nobody zoned, the old order reimagined from bedrock. Your rebellion wears work boots. It shows up early, builds the alternative, and lets the results argue. Slow genius, permanent output."
- k2_functional: "You express in built things: the model, the prototype, the standing proof."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Ground-breaking","Deadpan","Unconventional"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Talent":"Your talent is constructive genius: making real what others only pitch. It compounds with patience, so pick projects worth years. Your monuments will outlast every clever thing said about them.","Performance":"You perform through results: the opening day, the finished span, the harvest weighed. Let there be openings, invite people to what you built. Even mountains benefit from an unveiling.","Defiance":"Your defiance is seismic: rare, slow, landscape-changing. When you finally move against a structure, you replace it. Use that power on things that matter, not on every irritating fence."}

- Sibling cell 土_食神 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Good enough arrived years ago and you parked there. The skills plateaued where the applause got comfortable, the menu settled into rotation, the questions you ask the world got smaller. Nothing is wrong. That is the anesthetic, and it is working."

Core element Fire, energy element Earth. Law: Fire feeds Earth (火生土: ash becomes soil). Relative to the core the energy is the fed, so Earth is this core's Expression. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Earth on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Earth as the Expression is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. value.text: Pushing back is your first reply to almost anything. Because agreeing feels like giving something up, you push against a plan rather than check if you mind it. Keep in mind, pushing back costs you the same whether the plan was good or not.

value_b.text: You push back on a thing before you have looked at it. Disagreeing fits you better than nodding does, so you push first and judge later. You know that some of what you pushed against was on your side.

value.text: Saying too much is the honesty you were built for. A thought left unsaid feels like a lie to you, so you say the whole thing rather than the useful half. Remember that the useful half was the only part you were asked for.

value_b.text: You say the extra sentence, the one the moment did not need. Holding a thought in feels more dishonest than letting it out, so the clever version wins over the quiet one. You know saying less would have said the same thing.

value.text: Overdoing it is the only way you know to be sure of enough. Since plain and finished feels like settling, you make it bigger rather than call it done. You pay for the extra out of yourself, a price worth keeping in mind.

value_b.text: You overdo it on purpose, since enough never felt like a safe place to stop. Making it bigger is more your style than making it done, so every small job grows a second floor. Remember that the second floor comes out of your own supply.

value.text: Overdoing it is how you make sure a thing looks like you. Long after the plain version would do, you keep adding rather than finishing and spend what the end needed. You pay for every extra in the sleep the finish was owed.

value.text: You overdo it for people who asked for something modest. Since a plain job feels beneath what you can do, you hand them a bigger thing later instead of the small thing now. You owed them the small one now, the one with a use.
